notes: 2026-08-31 arm comparison. FIVE ARMS, each differing from arm0_ctl in EXACTLY ONE field, so any difference is attributable to that field. CMA is stochastic, so each cell is replicated over 3 seeds -- with one run per cell the arm effect could not be separated from seed noise. Two starts: 'base' (the positive control -- the only Aug-30 run that behaved cleanly) and 'fixture:seed2' (attracting orbit but fails contract C5 and C6, so RAMP, BRACK and FLOOR all have something to fix and C3/C4 are not confounds). Compare arms ONLY after re-scoring every endpoint on a COMMON yardstick -- fit.contract, plus c_ptc under arm0's objective -- because each arm minimises a different function and their own cost values are not comparable. P2 dose floor ONLY, 0.5 -> 0.01 x S_crit. Single-variable: n_dose and include_zero unchanged. Predicts C6 passes more often, at the cost of moving S_crit from the 25th to the 69th log-percentile of the window. BOUND IS 3.5, NOT THE 3.0 OF THE AUG-30 CAMPAIGN, AND UNIFORMLY SO ACROSS ALL FIVE ARMS. The promoted start sits at max|v_i| = 2.9996 in the basis it was fitted in -- ON the old boundary -- and the gauge-quotient basis is not reproducible (hazard 18), so a rotation puts one of its 16 components at 3.0317, marginally OUTSIDE. CMA then refuses the start outright. The box is therefore BASIS-DEPENDENT: 'inside the box' is not a property of the model. Raising it uniformly keeps every arm-to-arm contrast single-variable; it does mean arm0_ctl, not the Aug-30 campaign, is the control.
